Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Kitchen, meals & drinks

whole adjective

in one piece

also in one piece, intact, unbroken, swallow whole, complete, sound (healthy), sound (unharmed)

classical

Sen. Ep. 72.8: quidquid excēpit prōtinus integrum dēvorat
Cato Agr. 99: fīcī āridae sī volēs utī integrae sint
Cato Agr. 14.4: tēgula integra
Traupman 65: sound (in health)

integer, integra, integrum

declension

whole, intact, untouched

From in- and the root of tangō: “untouched” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • solidus, solida, solidum — whole, entire, not in parts

    declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 8.36: ut solidōs hauriant cervōs taurōsque (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 6.253: solida taurōrum vīscera (Lewis & Short)

    First of all “solid, not hollow”; “whole” as opposed to divided.

Examples

  • vīdistī aliquandō canem missa ā dominō frusta pānis aut carnis apertō ōre captantem? quidquid excēpit prōtinus integrum dēvorat

    have you ever seen a dog snapping open-mouthed at the scraps of bread or meat its master throws? whatever it catches it swallows whole at onceSen. Ep. 72.8

  • fīcī āridae sī volēs utī integrae sint, in vās fictile conditō

    if you want dried figs to keep whole, put them away in an earthenware jarCato Agr. 99

See also whole, half.

SourcesLewis & Short: integer · Lewis & Short: solidus
